title: null, undefined, and optional access interview drills

items.question: What is the difference between null and undefined?
items.answer: undefined is the default for uninitialized variables, missing properties, and functions with no return. null is an explicit assignment meaning intentionally empty. typeof null is "object" (legacy). null == undefined is true; === is false. JSON.stringify omits undefined keys but keeps null.
followUps: How do default parameters treat null vs undefined?
items.sixtySeconds: undefined unset; null intentional. typeof null object bug. == pairs them; === not. JSON drops undefined.

items.question: How does optional chaining differ from logical AND guards?
items.answer: ?. short-circuits when base is null or undefined, returning undefined without TypeError. It works for property, bracket, and call access. && stops on any falsy base including 0 and "". ?. does not validate data shape — typos still return undefined silently.
items.sixtySeconds: ?. nullish only. && any falsy. Short-circuit safe navigation. Not schema validation.

items.question: When do you use ?? instead of ||?
items.answer: ?? replaces only null or undefined. || replaces any falsy value including 0, empty string, false, and NaN. Use ?? for numeric and string defaults where 0 or "" are valid. Mixing ?? and || without parentheses is SyntaxError.
followUps: What does count || 10 do when count is 0?
items.sixtySeconds: ?? nullish only. || all falsy. port 0 example. Parens when mixing.

items.question: How do you defend against bad JSON at an API boundary?
items.answer: JSON.parse returns any shape — TypeScript types erase at run time. Validate required fields with typeof and explicit null checks; throw TypeError or domain ValidationError. Use guard clauses for early exit. Apply ?. and ?? only after shape is proven for optional nested fields.
followUps: Why is TS not enough alone?
items.sixtySeconds: Parse then validate. Guards at edge. TS erased. ?. optional only after required proven.

items.question: Compare JavaScript null safety to TypeScript strictNullChecks and C# NRT.
items.answer: JavaScript enforces nothing at compile time — null and undefined exist at run time. TypeScript strictNullChecks adds compile warnings; emitted JS has no checks unless you write them. C# NRT warns on nullable references. All three need runtime validation on external JSON. Avoid TS non-null assertion ! without proof.
items.sixtySeconds: JS runtime only. TS/C# compile. JSON validate always. ! assertion dangerous. Three layers: compile ?. ?? guards.
